kit.title: Small-Nonprofit Restricted Grant & Audit Readiness Kit
kit.summary: Reconciles ledger rows against restricted grant line items, lists missing receipt attachments as explicit nulls instead of zeros, and drafts narrative variance notes for treasurer review.

steps.title: Recompute restricted grant spend by budget category
steps.guidance: Sum posted expenses per grant code, flag unreceipted rows as missing, and compute remaining restricted balance.

steps.title: Draft quarterly grant progress and variance summary
steps.guidance: Summarize completed deliverables and flag any line variance above 10% for budget-modification review.

steps.title: Approve restricted-fund allocation and variance treatment
steps.guidance: Review every flagged receipt gap and approve any cost-reallocation request.

steps.title: File signed report in funder or regulator portal
steps.guidance: External portal submissions and 990 schedules are filed only by an authorized officer.

skill.name: restricted-grant-reconciler
skill.description: Reconciles nonprofit ledger rows against restricted grant budgets without inventing missing numbers.
skill.instructions: Check each expense row's grant tag, date window, and receipt attachment status. Report missing receipts as null/unverified rather than zero, highlight budget lines with >10% variance, and output a review packet for the board treasurer.
refuses: Estimating or inventing missing receipt amounts
Submitting grant reports or tax filings externally

tool.name: check_grant_budget_variance
tool.description: Computes line-by-line restricted grant spend, remaining balance, variance percent, and missing-receipt count.

checklist: Verify every expense date falls inside the grant agreement's start and end dates.
Keep unreceipted transactions in a separate 'pending documentation' list instead of counting them as cleared.
Require board treasurer sign-off before requesting a budget-line modification above 10%.

sources.title: IRS Compliance Guide for 501(c)(3) Public Charities (Publication 4221-PC)

kit.title: Coerced Overseas Offer Helpline Directory & Safe Triage Kit
kit.summary: Matches corridor countries and languages to re-verified public helplines and consular desks, surfacing unverified offer indicators while reserving all crisis safety planning for trained staff.

steps.title: Match corridor country and caller language to verified public hotlines
steps.guidance: Return only helpline entries whose checked_date is within 90 days; mark older entries for human re-verification.

steps.title: Live conversation with caller or family member
steps.guidance: Conduct trauma-informed intake without automated scripts speaking to the caller.

steps.title: Crisis safety and consular escalation plan
steps.guidance: Handle any immediate safety risk directly with trained human responders.

steps.title: Transmit warm referral to consular or partner desk
steps.guidance: Send referral details only with explicit consent and human supervisor review.

skill.name: corridor-helpline-lookup
skill.description: Finds verified public helplines and consular contacts by corridor and language, flagging stale entries before use.
skill.instructions: Look up matching corridor helplines from the verified JSON directory, display each entry's last checked date and official URL, and immediately route any active distress call to a human responder without generating safety advice.
refuses: Generating exit or safety instructions for a person at risk
Collecting or logging caller location coordinates

tool.name: match_verified_helplines
tool.description: Filters verified public helpline records by destination country, origin country, and spoken language.

checklist: Check whether every listed helpline number was verified within the past 90 days before handing it to a caller.
Note transit changes such as a ticket routed to a border town different from the stated office city.
Escalate any live safety concern immediately to the human shift lead.

kit.title: Monthly Program Impact Report Kit
kit.summary: Turns a month of program records into an impact report: totals by measure, change from last month, results against targets, and missing numbers kept as unknown. The program manager checks every figure, and the executive director approves the report and shares it.
kit.target_org: Community nonprofit reporting monthly results to its board and partners

steps.title: Total the month's program records by measure
steps.guidance: Total sessions, people served and outcome check-ins for the month by measure, compare each with the month's target and with last month, and keep any missing count as unknown, never zero.

steps.title: Draft the monthly impact report
steps.guidance: Draft the report's sections: highlights, results against targets, changes from last month, what staff are watching, and next month. Every number comes from the results table, and no participant is quoted without staff approval.

steps.title: Check every figure against the program records
steps.guidance: The program manager traces each figure to the program's own records and corrects or removes any figure that cannot be traced.

steps.title: Approve the report and how shortfalls are explained
steps.guidance: The executive director decides how shortfalls and changes are explained and approves the report.

steps.title: Share the report with the board and partners
steps.guidance: The executive director shares the approved report with the board and partners. The agent never sends or publishes the report.

skills.name: impact-report-drafter
skills.description: Drafts a monthly impact report from a results table, keeping every number traced to a measure and every gap visible.
skills.instructions: Use the outline's sections and word limits: highlights, results against targets, changes from last month, what staff are watching, and next month. Take every number from the results table and cite its measure. Write missing numbers as not yet counted, and name the site they are missing from. Describe what was done and counted in plain words at an eighth-grade reading level, and never claim an outcome the records do not show. Use a participant quote only when staff have marked it approved, never with a name or a detail that could identify the person. Flag every measure below 90 percent of its target for the executive director's explanation.
refuses: Inventing or estimating a missing number
Claiming outcomes the records do not show
Quoting a participant without staff approval
Sharing the report outside the organization

tools.name: summarize_month_by_measure
tools.description: Totals a month's program records by measure and compares each with its target and with last month, listing missing counts as unknown.

artifacts.name: monthly_results_table
artifacts.title: Monthly Results Table
artifacts.summary: One row per measure for the month: target, count, percent of target, last month, change and the record it came from. No participant details.

artifacts.name: impact_report_outline
artifacts.title: Monthly Impact Report Outline
artifacts.summary: Five-section outline for the monthly report, with every number drawn from the results table.
spec: 1. Highlights: three plain sentences, each with its measure.
2. Results against targets, from the results table only.
3. Changes from last month, from the results table only.
4. What staff are watching, written or approved by the program manager.

checklist: Every number in the report traces to a row in the results table.
Missing counts read as not yet counted, never as zero.
Participant quotes appear only with staff approval and never with a name.
The program manager checks figures before the executive director approves the report.

sources.title: eCFR: 2 CFR 200.329, Monitoring and reporting program performance
National Council of Nonprofits: Administration and Financial Management

kit.title: Community Services Warm-Referral & HSDS Triage Kit
kit.summary: Matches Open Referral HSDS service listings against household needs, flags missing paperwork early, and drafts a plain-language warm-referral note for caseworker approval.

steps.title: Filter published local programs by hours, language, and service category
steps.guidance: Show matching programs alongside required documents and current intake hours.

steps.title: Draft plain-language warm-referral summary
steps.guidance: Prepare a concise referral checklist in the resident's preferred language for the caseworker to inspect.

steps.title: In-person or phone intake conversation
steps.guidance: Discuss household priorities, consent, and accessibility needs directly with the resident.

steps.title: Confirm program fit and referral selection
steps.guidance: Never let an automated filter deny a resident; the navigator confirms every referral.

skill.name: warm-referral-drafter
skill.description: Matches Open Referral HSDS program entries and drafts a plain-language checklist for a human navigator to review.
skill.instructions: Given published HSDS program records and a synthetic or navigator-entered need summary, list candidate programs with hours, transit notes, and required documents. Mark uncertain requirements as 'ask desk to confirm' rather than excluding the resident.
refuses: Transmitting client details externally without navigator sign-off

tool.name: filter_hsds_services
tool.description: Queries Open Referral HSDS service entries by category, zip/postal prefix, and language support.

checklist: Confirm whether the partner pantry or clinic requires photo ID or accepts self-attestation of address.
Check language interpretation availability before scheduling a warm handoff.
Obtain explicit resident consent before sharing any referral note with a partner nonprofit.

kit.title: Overseas Contract & Agency Fee Arithmetic Intake Kit
kit.summary: Computes total placement fees as a share of first-month wages, flags contract pay reductions, and prepares a structured summary for a trained caseworker without accusing any party.

steps.title: List stated wage, deductions, and fee receipts
steps.guidance: Extract each amount with its currency code and document line reference; leave missing figures null.

steps.title: Confidential intake conversation with the worker
steps.guidance: Confirm whether documents or passports are held and what the worker wishes to do next.

steps.title: Caseworker referral or legal-aid decision
steps.guidance: Decide with the worker whether to request missing records, seek fee recovery, or close intake.

skill.name: recruitment-fee-intake-check
skill.description: Prepares a neutral arithmetic table comparing job-offer pay, contract pay, and fee receipts for an NGO caseworker.
skill.instructions: Read only synthetic or client-consented local text inside the NGO's own workspace. List every fee and wage with its ISO currency code, compute fee share of first-month pay when currencies match, cite the applicable statute section, and stop before any interview or legal recommendation.
refuses: Contacting an agency, lender, or employer
Calling any person or firm a lawbreaker
Recommending an action without caseworker review

tool.name: compute_fee_to_wage_ratio
tool.description: Computes placement fees as a percentage of first-month contract pay when currencies match and compares against a statutory cap.

checklist: Verify that all fee receipts and contract wages share the same ISO currency before computing a ratio.
Record whether a second contract changed the monthly wage promised in the initial job advertisement.
Hand every case mentioning identity-document retention combined with loan deductions straight to a trained caseworker.

kit.title: Community Pantry Shift Onboarding & Incident Escalation SOP Pack
kit.summary: Standalone SOP playbook and multilingual role-card drafting skill for volunteer coordinators, reserving all medical, safety, and accommodation decisions strictly for the on-site shift captain.
kit.target_org: Neighborhood mutual-aid pantry and cold-weather shelter

steps.title: Generate printable station checklists and shift handoff notes
steps.guidance: Prepare plain-language station cards (receiving, sorting, distribution, cleanup) with clear escalation contact boxes.

steps.title: Handle accommodation requests and volunteer conduct
steps.guidance: Any conflict or guest accommodation decision is handled in person by the trained shift captain.

steps.title: Execute live medical, weather, or physical safety response
steps.actor: On-site shift captain and certified first-aid lead
steps.guidance: Immediate physical safety or medical distress is handled directly by on-site human responders.

steps.title: Send approved shift schedule and emergency contacts to volunteers
steps.guidance: Coordinator reviews and sends shift packets directly; agents never message volunteers automatically.

skills.name: shift-role-card-drafter
skills.description: Drafts concise, accessible volunteer station cards and shift handoff checklists from a pantry or shelter's operating hours and station list.
skills.instructions: Format each station card at an 8th-grade reading level with three sections: Setup, During Shift, and When to Call the Shift Captain. Never generate medical advice or disciplinary decisions.
refuses: Making volunteer disciplinary or dismissal decisions
Generating clinical or emergency medical instructions

artifacts.name: shift_escalation_sop
artifacts.title: Three-Tier On-Site Escalation Playbook
artifacts.summary: Printable escalation tree distinguishing routine supply restocks from immediate human shift-captain and emergency-responder triggers.
spec: Tier 1 (Station Lead): Restock shortages, queue pacing, translation card lookup.
Tier 2 (Human Shift Captain -- immediate): Guest accommodation request, interpersonal dispute, minor facility hazard.
Tier 3 (Human Shift Captain + Local Emergency Services): Medical distress or immediate physical safety concern.

artifacts.name: station_handoff_template
artifacts.title: End-of-Shift Handoff CSV Template
artifacts.summary: Zero-PII station handoff log recording supply counts, equipment status, and open follow-ups for the next coordinator.

checklist: Confirm the on-site shift captain's name and phone extension are filled in before printing station cards.
Verify no guest or volunteer personal health details appear in shift handoff notes.
Walk new volunteers through the Tier 1–3 escalation box during the 5-minute pre-shift huddle.
